abstract: |
  The [R]{.proglang} package [tidyfinance]{.pkg} provides research infrastructure for the empirical asset pricing data workflow. This workflow turns raw accounting and return data into factor portfolios for asset pricing tests, optimal portfolio allocation, and the design of trading strategies. [tidyfinance]{.pkg} exposes every construction decision as a configurable parameter with a documented default. A unified `download_data()` interface covers WRDS (CRSP, Compustat), Ken French's Data Library, FRED, and other sources, and applies provider-specific cleaning. Modular functions automate fiscal-year lagging, breakpoint computation, and portfolio aggregation. We illustrate the package by reproducing the asset growth factor end-to-end from raw data. Researchers who want precomputed series instead of rebuilding the pipeline can download a factor library of `{r} format(dplyr::n_distinct(tidyfinance::download_data("tidyfinance", "factor_library_grid")$sorting_variable), big.mark = ",")` sorting variables across `{r} format(tidyfinance::download_data("tidyfinance", "factor_library_grid") |> nrow(), big.mark = ",")` specifications with a single `download_data()` call or browse the time series at [factors.tidy-finance.org](https://factors.tidy-finance.org).
keywords: [financial risk factors, reproducible research, asset pricing, R]

  d <- as.Date(d)
  day <- as.integer(format(d, "%d"))
  suffix <- if (day %% 100 %in% 11:13) {
    "th"
  } else {
    switch(as.character(day %% 10), "1" = "st", "2" = "nd", "3" = "rd", "th")
  }
  paste0(format(d, "%B "), day, suffix, ", ", format(d, "%Y"))
}

## Introduction {#sec-intro}

Factor returns enter empirical asset pricing tests, optimal portfolio allocation, and risk-management decisions. Producing factor returns is a three-stage pipeline: data acquisition (e.g., downloading and cleaning raw accounting and return data from the Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP), Compustat, and similar providers); variable construction (lagging variables to avoid look-ahead bias); and portfolio sorting (assigning securities to portfolios by characteristic). Each stage embeds construction choices: how to handle delistings, which fiscal-year lag to apply, where to set breakpoints, whether to equal- or value-weight portfolios. Few pipelines are standardized, and fewer still ship with executable code. Anyone who reproduces or extends a factor series therefore reconstructs the pipeline from scratch, with no way to verify that the result matches the published series.

No widely adopted tool covers this upstream workflow. The most popular factor sources publish *series* without the code that produced them: Ken French's Data Library [@fama.2023] supplies the Fama-French three- and five-factor returns and dozens of sorted portfolios. Other projects do release code: the Open Source Bond Asset Pricing project [@dickerson.2023], available at [openbondassetpricing.com](https://openbondassetpricing.com/), covers fixed income; the Open Source Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing repository [@chen.2022] reproduces 213+ published anomalies, and @jensen.2023 release a global factor library spanning hundreds of long-short signals across many countries. None of these sources, however, exposes the preprocessing pipeline as configurable code that researchers can inspect or modify. Many individual authors also host their own published factors, with transparency about construction choices varying widely. Existing [R]{.proglang} packages for quantitative finance operate downstream of factor construction, on price and return panels the user must already have. Between raw data and standard asset pricing tests sits an opaque layer, where construction choices accumulate silently.

This paper introduces [tidyfinance]{.pkg}, an [R]{.proglang} package on CRAN that exposes each stage of the pipeline as configurable code. The package addresses each stage with a dedicated interface. A unified `download_data()` function cleans, aligns, and harmonizes panels from WRDS (CRSP, Compustat, TRACE, FISD), Ken French's Data Library, FRED, and seven other providers, including current constituents for `{r} format(nrow(tidyfinance::list_supported_indexes()), big.mark = ",")` major equity indexes; @tbl-data-sources catalogs the full set. Composable helpers then automate fiscal-year lagging, breakpoint computation, and portfolio aggregation. Every construction choice is exposed as a function argument with a default that follows established convention (for instance, value-weights and the Fama-French fiscal-year lag). A default call reproduces standard practice; overriding any default takes one argument.

We illustrate the package by reproducing the asset growth factor of @cooper.2008 end-to-end from raw CRSP and Compustat data, then varying any construction choice with a single-argument change. To spare researchers the work of rebuilding the pipeline, we run [tidyfinance]{.pkg} across many defensible combinations and publish the results as a factor library of `{r} format(nrow(sorting_variable_information), big.mark = ",")` sorting variables across `{r} format(nrow(portfolio_sort_grid), big.mark = ",")` specifications. The library is available through a single `download_data()` call or an interactive dashboard at [factors.tidy-finance.org](https://factors.tidy-finance.org). The workflow that the package operationalizes is developed in the open-access textbooks *Tidy Finance with [R]{.proglang}* [@scheuch.2023] and *Tidy Finance with [Python]{.proglang}* [@scheuch.2024], which present each step in tutorial form with inline scripts. The contribution of this paper is the [tidyfinance]{.pkg} CRAN package itself: a unified, configurable, tested, and versioned [R]{.proglang} API for that workflow. Where the books teach a reader how to assemble the pipeline from scratch, the package supplies it as a single dependency that researchers can call, audit, and reuse without rebuilding the underlying code.

## Background and related work {#sec-background}

The [R]{.proglang} ecosystem for empirical asset pricing splits cleanly into three groups. Each addresses one slice of the workflow and leaves the rest to the user.

**Data-acquisition packages.** Several [R]{.proglang} packages retrieve specific data sources commonly used in asset pricing. [frenchdata]{.pkg} [@frenchdata.2021] downloads and parses the zip archives from Ken French's Data Library into long data frames; it does not touch WRDS and does not implement any construction step beyond reading the published factor series. [quantmod]{.pkg} [@ryan.2025] and [tidyquant]{.pkg} [@dancho.2026] cover Yahoo Finance, FRED, and Tiingo, returning daily open, high, low, and close price series and a small set of derived return helpers; neither connects to WRDS, and neither covers factor-construction logic. [Rblpapi]{.pkg} [@armstrong.Rblpapi] queries the Bloomberg terminal for subscribers; the returned series leave the same factor-construction gap unfilled as the packages above. None of these packages covers the WRDS-CRSP-Compustat panel or the cleaning, alignment, and survivorship conventions the asset-pricing literature requires.

**Downstream analysis packages.** Once a cleaned panel is in hand, several packages support analysis. [PerformanceAnalytics]{.pkg} [@peterson.2026] computes performance and risk metrics for return series. [fPortfolio]{.pkg} [@wuertz.fPortfolio] covers portfolio optimization. [RQuantLib]{.pkg} [@eddelbuettel.RQuantLib] interfaces with QuantLib for derivative pricing. [highfrequency]{.pkg} [@boudt.highfrequency] cleans intraday trade-and-quote panels and implements microstructure-volatility estimators; it operates on a panel the user must already have. Each of these tools assumes that the panel of returns and factors is already constructed; none implements a factor-construction layer.

**Factor data releases.** A group of projects publishes *factor return series* directly. Ken French's Data Library [@fama.2023] supplies the canonical Fama-French three- and five-factor returns and dozens of sorted portfolios, but documents construction in prose only; no construction code is released. @akey.2026 show that these series change retroactively as the underlying methodology is silently revised, so that the factor returns a researcher obtains depend on *when* they were downloaded, with material effects on mutual-fund performance and cross-sectional asset pricing tests---precisely the opacity that a transparent, code-first pipeline removes. Three more recent projects pair the published factor data with the construction script that produced it. @hou.2020 replicate 452 cross-sectional anomalies and document that most fail out-of-sample, attributing the failures in part to undocumented construction variation across studies. The Open Source Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing repository [@chen.2022] responds by publishing per-anomaly construction scripts alongside the resulting 213+ long-short returns. The Open Source Bond Asset Pricing project [@dickerson.2023] does the same for corporate bond factors. @jensen.2023 release the Global Factor Data of hundreds of long-short signals across many countries, together with the construction code in [Python]{.proglang}. These projects represent a substantial move toward transparency: a reader can inspect exactly how each factor was built and reproduce its returns. Two limitations remain. First, none exposes the pipeline as a callable API. A user who wants the asset growth factor rebalanced in January instead of July, or formed on NYSE-plus-NASDAQ breakpoints, or computed on a different fiscal-year lag, must fork the published script and edit it by hand. The script is not a function with named arguments. Second, the factor returns are frozen at the release date, with no in-workflow path to refresh them as new WRDS observations arrive or as a researcher's design choices evolve.

**Tidy finance: transparency and modularity.** [tidyfinance]{.pkg} fills the missing middle: it supplies the cleaned WRDS-CRSP-Compustat panel that data-acquisition packages do not produce and exposes the factor-construction pipeline that downstream analysis packages assume to be in hand. One `download_data()` call returns a cleaned WRDS-CRSP-Compustat panel; further functions implement the full factor-construction pipeline (fiscal-year lagging, breakpoint computation, portfolio sorting, long-short aggregation) as a chain of composable steps whose arguments cover the construction choices that vary across studies in the literature above. The companion textbooks *Tidy Finance with [R]{.proglang}* [@scheuch.2023] and *Tidy Finance with [Python]{.proglang}* [@scheuch.2024] develop the workflow itself in tutorial form, with the construction steps written out as inline scripts for readers to follow. The package is the software artifact that turns that workflow into a CRAN library: tested, versioned, and callable as a single dependency rather than copied chunk by chunk into each new project. Two design principles, both inherited from the textbooks, guide the API. *Transparency*: every construction decision is exposed as a configurable parameter with a documented default, following the *tidy data* discipline of @wickham.2014. *Modularity*: each construction step is a small function, so researchers can chain the full pipeline or call individual pieces inside their own workflows. [tidyfinance]{.pkg} additionally covers asset pricing tests and optimal portfolio choice; this paper focuses on factor construction and defers the remaining functionality to dedicated treatments.

## Package overview {#sec-overview}

### Installation and setup {#sec-installation}

You can install the released version of [tidyfinance]{.pkg} [from CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=tidyfinance) via:

```{r}
#| label: install-tidyfinance-cran
#| eval: false
install.packages("tidyfinance")
```

To install the development version of [tidyfinance]{.pkg} from [GitHub](https://github.com/tidy-finance/r-tidyfinance), first install [pak]{.pkg}, then run:

```{r}
#| label: install-tidyfinance-dev
#| eval: false
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("tidy-finance/r-tidyfinance")
```

Once installed, load the package with: 
```{r}
#| label: load-tidyfinance-initial
library("tidyfinance")
```

### Design and workflow {#sec-design}

The empirical asset pricing workflow decomposes into three stages: data acquisition, variable construction, and portfolio sorting. Each stage involves dozens of small decisions: universe filters, cleaning rules, rebalancing conventions, breakpoint definitions. @tbl-functions catalogs the user-facing functions exported by [tidyfinance]{.pkg}, grouped by workflow stage. The remainder of this section walks through them in narrative order.

+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Function                                 | Purpose                                                             |
+==========================================+=====================================================================+
| *Data acquisition*                                                                                             |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `download_data()`                        | Retrieves and cleans a panel from supported data providers.         |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `set_wrds_credentials()`                 | Stores WRDS username and password in `.Renviron` for subsequent     |
|                                          | calls.                                                              |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| *Variable construction*                                                                                        |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `add_lagged_columns()`                   | Attaches the most recent observed value within a configurable       |
|                                          | look-back window, with optional Fama-French timing.                 |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `join_lagged_values()`                   | Merges lagged values from a source panel into a target panel using  |
|                                          | the same windowing logic.                                           |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `winsorize()`                            | Replaces values outside the $q$-th and $(1-q)$-th percentiles with  |
|                                          | the corresponding quantile.                                         |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `trim()`                                 | Sets values outside the $q$-th and $(1-q)$-th percentiles to `NA`.  |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `compute_rolling_value()`                | Applies an aggregation function over a calendar-time rolling        |
|                                          | window.                                                             |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| *Portfolio sorting*                                                                                            |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `compute_breakpoints()`                  | Computes quantile cutoffs from a cross-section, optionally          |
|                                          | restricted by exchange or by minimum market-cap quantile.           |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `assign_portfolio()`                     | Maps each observation to a portfolio integer using supplied or      |
|                                          | computed breakpoints.                                               |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `compute_portfolio_returns()`            | Forms portfolios period by period and returns equal-, value-, and   |
|                                          | capped-value-weighted return panels.                                |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `compute_long_short_returns()`           | Computes the top-minus-bottom (or bottom-minus-top) spread from     |
|                                          | the output of `compute_portfolio_returns()`.                        |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `implement_portfolio_sort()`             | Wraps filtering, breakpoint computation, assignment, and            |
|                                          | aggregation into a single call for univariate and bivariate sorts.  |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| *Asset pricing tests*                                                                                          |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `estimate_fama_macbeth()`                | Runs cross-sectional ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions each  |
|                                          | period and aggregates into average risk premia with Newey-West      |
|                                          | standard errors [@newey.1987].                                      |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `estimate_betas()`                       | Estimates rolling-window market betas for each asset.               |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `estimate_model()`                       | Fits a linear model from a formula string and returns the           |
|                                          | coefficients as a tidy one-row data frame.                          |
+------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+

: User-facing functions in [tidyfinance]{.pkg}, grouped by workflow stage. Functions whose first argument is a panel chain naturally via the native pipe `|>`; `breakpoint_options()`, `filter_options()`, `portfolio_sort_options()`, and `data_options()` (explained in detail below) bundle the configurable arguments for the sorting helpers. {#tbl-functions}

### Data acquisition {#sec-data-access}

[tidyfinance]{.pkg} exposes one interface, `download_data()`, to `{r} format(nrow(tidyfinance::list_supported_datasets()), big.mark = ",")` datasets: equity returns, fixed-income transactions, macroeconomic predictors, index constituents, and more. @tbl-data-sources lists all available sources. `list_supported_datasets()` returns the full catalog programmatically. The companion [Python]{.proglang} package [tidyfinance]{.pkg}, hosted on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tidyfinance/), exposes the same `download_data()` interface, with identical signatures and dataset identifiers, so analyses can be ported between the two languages without changes to the data layer.

```{=latex}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
```

|                |                                    | ```                                     |

|                |                                    | ```                                     |

+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+

+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+

|                |                                    |     "high_frequency_sp500")             |
|                |                                    | ```                                     |

| Risk-Free Rate | Monthly risk-free rate             | ```                                     |

+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
| Factor Library | Precomputed factor returns         | ```                                     |
|                | across construction choices        | download_data(                          |
|                |                                    |   domain = "tidyfinance",               |
|                |                                    |   dataset = "factor_library",           |
|                |                                    |   sorting_variable = "ag")              |
|                |                                    | ```                                     |
+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
| **WRDS (subscription required)**                                                              |
+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
| CRSP           | Daily and monthly stock returns,   | ```                                     |
|                | market cap, listing exchange,      | download_data(                          |
|                | industry information               |   domain = "wrds",                      |
|                |                                    |   dataset = "crsp_monthly")             |
|                |                                    | ```                                     |
+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
| Compustat      | Annual and quarterly financial     | ```                                     |
|                | statements                         | download_data(                          |
|                |                                    |   domain = "wrds",                      |
|                |                                    |   dataset = "compustat_annual")         |
|                |                                    | ```                                     |
+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
| CCM Links      | CRSP-Compustat linking table       | ```                                     |
|                | (permno to gvkey)                  | download_data(                          |
|                |                                    |   domain = "wrds",                      |
|                |                                    |   dataset = "ccm_links")                |
|                |                                    | ```                                     |
+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
| FISD           | Mergent Fixed Income               | ```                                     |
|                | Securities Database                | download_data(                          |
|                |                                    |   domain = "wrds",                      |
|                |                                    |   dataset = "fisd")                     |
|                |                                    | ```                                     |
+----------------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
| TRACE          | Corporate bond transactions        | ```                                     |
|                | (Dick-Nielsen cleaned)             | download_data(                          |
|                |                                    |   domain = "wrds",                      |
